1.note: Here and throughout the chapter, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

2.note: See how you translated the nearly identical idiom in 1:2.
The word **Lift up** is singular here because God is speaking to Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase **sons of** refers to male descendants. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [male descendants of Kohath from the midst of the male descendants of Levi]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if Kohath’s descendants were physically located **from the midst of** the other Levites. He means that they should be counted from among all the Levites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly.

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase **house of their fathers** refers to largest divisions within a single tribe. The word **clans** refers to the largest divisions of each **house of their fathers**. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers made up of those clans]
See how you translated this phrase in 1:2.

3.q: מִ⁠בֶּ֨ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה וְ⁠עַ֖ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה
3.note: Here and throughout this chapter, this phrase identifies men who are at least 30 years old and no older than 50 years old. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [men who are 30–50 years old]

The expression **who comes to** is a common expression of his culture to mean “who is able to be part of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [one who is able to be part of the army]

Here, Moses is speaking of the group who works in the tent of meeting as if it were an **army**. See the chapter introduction for more information. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the group of workers]

4.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [This is how the sons of Kohath serve]

The expression **the holy of the holies** is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language.

Here, **the holy of the holies** represents the most holy things or objects. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the things that are most holy]

5.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put **Aaron and his sons** together at the beginning of the clause, rather than having **Aaron** first and **his sons** later. Alternate translation: [And Aaron and his sons shall come]

Here, **camp** represents the people living in the camp. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people in the camp]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that **the veil of the curtain** refers to the special curtain that separated the Most Holy Place from the rest of the sacred tent. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the veil of the curtain in front of the Holy of Holies]

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **veil** that is characterized by being a **curtain**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the curtain that is a veil]

6.note: The pronoun **it** refers to the Box of the Testimony. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [on the box and the curtain covering it]

This phrase refers to high-quality leather made from the skin of an animal. The animal may be a **porpoise**, a type of sea creature with leathery skin. See the chapter introduction for more information. If your readers would not be familiar with this type of sea animal, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [durable animal skin]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **cloth** that is characterized by being **completely blue**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an entirely blue cloth]

The implication is that the blue cloth should be placed over all the other coverings that were put on the Box of the Testimony. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on top of all these things]

The implication is that these **poles** were inserted into rings on the sides of the ark and used to carry it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the box in order to carry it]

7.note: The phrase **the table of the faces** is a common expression of this culture that means “the table that is in Yahweh’s presence.” This table was placed before Yahweh in the tent of meeting, and the Levites were to place special bread on it for Yahweh, as described in Exodus 25:30. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the table in Yahweh’s presence]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **cloth of blue** that is characterized by **blue**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a cloth that is blue]

7.q: אֶת־הַ⁠קְּעָרֹ֤ת וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠כַּפֹּת֙ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠מְּנַקִּיֹּ֔ת וְ⁠אֵ֖ת קְשׂ֣וֹת הַ⁠נָּ֑סֶךְ
7.note: The **dishes**, **palm-sized bowls**, **bowls**, and **pitchers** are different kinds of vessels used in the tabernacle service. If your readers would not be familiar with what these vessels are, you could use the names of similar containers that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [the plates and the large spoons and the containers and the jars of the drink offering]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **pitchers** that are used for **the drink offering**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the pitchers used with drink offerings]

The phrase **bread of continuity** refers to the bread that was regularly offered to God. If your readers would not be familiar with what this bread is, you could use a term that shows it was bread that was always present on the table as an offering to God. Alternate translation: [and the bread of continuity offered to me]

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the bread** that was characterized by being offered regularly (in **continuity**). If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the bread that is offered continually]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **continuity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the continual bread]

By **shall be on it**, Yahweh means that the bread was to remain on the table when the priests covered it. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [shall stay on it]

8.note: Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **cloth** that was dyed by a **worm of scarlet**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a cloth dyed by worm of scarlet]

The expression **worm of scarlet** is a common expression of this culture that means “red” or “crimson.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [scarlet]
See how you translated the same phrase in 4:6.

The implication is that the poles were placed through the rings attached to the sides of the table so people could use them to carry it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the table in order to carry it]

9.note: See how you translated this phrase in 4:7.

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the lampstand** that produces **light**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the lampstand that produces light]

9.q: וְ⁠אֶת־נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֶת־מַלְקָחֶ֖י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֶת־מַחְתֹּתֶ֑י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֵת֙ כָּל־כְּלֵ֣י שַׁמְנָ֔⁠הּ
9.note: The **tongs** and **trays** are tools used to handle hot lamp wicks. The **lamps** burned olive oil, and the **vessels** contained that oil. If your readers would not be familiar with these items, you could use the names of similar tools that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [and its oil lamps and its wick tools and its wick plates and all the containers of its oil]

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the vessels** that contained **its oil**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vessels that contained its oil]

10.note: The implication is that the poles were used for carrying the items. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall attach them to a long piece of wood in order to carry them]

11.note: The term **altar of gold** assumes that readers will know this was the altar used for burning incense. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the incense altar of gold]

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the altar** that is characterized by being overlaid with **gold**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the altar overlaid with gold]
See how you translated this phrase in 4:7.

By **set its poles**, Yahweh means they put the poles into the rings that were on the sides of the altar so that they could carry it. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar use of this clause in 4:6. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the altar in order to carry it]

12.note: It might seem that the expression **the vessels of the ministry with which they minister** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [the vessels with which they minister]
See how you translated this phrase in 4:7.

By **put them on the carrying pole**, Yahweh means they must attach these items to poles that people will use to carry them. See how you translated this clause in 4:10. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and they shall attach them to a long piece of wood in order to carry them]

13.note: By **remove the ashes**, Yahweh means that the priests were to clean out the fat and ashes that remained after burning the sacrifices on the altar. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And they shall cleanse the altar of fat and ashes]

The text **the altar** refers to the bronze altar used for sacrifices that was placed in front of the tent of meeting. Yahweh assumes that readers will know which altar this is, since there were two altars used in worship. You could say this explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the sacrificial altar]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **cloth** that is characterized by **purple**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a cloth that is purple]

14.note: The **trays** were like large, flat plates and were used for holding meat and other things. The **meat forks** were used to stab and move the meat. The **shovels** and **basins** were used for moving and storing ashes, blood, and anything else. If your readers would not be familiar with these tools, you could use the names of similar things that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [the platters, the utensils for stabbing meat and the scoops and the containers]

It might seem that the expression **the basins—all the vessels of the altar** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [and the basins]

The implied meaning is that the poles were put into rings on the sides of the altar so that people could use them to carry it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar use of this clause in 4:6. Alternate translation: [and they shall slide poles into the rings on the sides of the altar in order to carry it]

15.note: The phrase **shall finish to cover** is a common expression of this culture that means “shall finish covering.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Aaron and his sons shall finish covering]

Here, **the camp** represents the people who are in the camp. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated this clause in 4:5. Alternate translation: [when the people in the camp set out]

Here, **the holy place** represents the sacred objects that belong in the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and they shall not touch the things that belong in the holy place]

The words **and die** express the result of touching the holy place. If it would be more natural in your language, you could make this connection more explicit. Alternate translation: [which would cause them to die]

The phrase **the burden of** refers to the objects that the sons of Kohath were responsible for carrying when the Israelites traveled. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [These are the things that must be carried by the sons of Kohath]

16.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **oversight**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And what is overseen by Eleazer … and he oversees]

Here Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the oil** as oil that produces **light**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the oil that is burned to produce light]

The phrase **incense of the spices** is using the possessive form to describe **incense** that is made out of **spices**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the incense that is made of spices]

The phrase **the grain offering of continuity** refers to a grain offering that is characterized by **continuity**—it was offered regularly. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated the same use of **continuity** in 4:7. Alternate translation: [and the grain offering that is offered continually]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **continuity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the continual grain offering]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **the oil** that is used for **anointing**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the oil that is used for anointing]

It might seem that the expression **the oversight of all the Dwelling** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [and all the Dwelling]

The implication is that this refers to everything that is contained in the **Dwelling**, **holy place**, and **vessels**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and everything that is in it, and everything that is in the holy place, and everything that is in its vessels]

Here, **holy place** represents the things that belong in the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:15. Alternate translation: [in the things that belong in the holy place]

18.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **tribe** that is made up of the **clans of the Kohathite**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the tribe that is made up of the clans of]

Here, **tribe** represents the descendants of Kohath who comprise part of the tribe. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the portion of the tribe of]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **Kohathite**. He means all the members of the Kohathite clan in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Kohathites]

Here, Moses is speaking as if the Kohathites were objects that could be physically removed **from the midst of** the Levites. He means that they could be eliminated as a group from among the Levites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [so that they no longer exist among]

19.note: The pronoun **this** refers to the instructions that follow about how Aaron and his sons must assign specific tasks to each of the Kohathites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But here is what you must]

The phrases **live** and **not die** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and they will certainly live]

Here, **and they will live** marks this clause as the purpose of Aaron and his sons showing each man what to carry. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that they will live]

Here, **holy of the holies** represents the most sacred items. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the things that are most holy]

By **shall go**, Yahweh means Aaron and his sons will enter the sacred tent to show each Kohathite man what he should carry. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [shall enter the sacred tent]

The phrase **set them man by man** is a common expression of this culture that means “to assign each person his own task.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and appoint each of them]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what he does to serve]
See how you translated the same use of **burden** in 4:15.

20.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the sons of Kohath. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But the sons of Kohath shall not go]

The implication is that the Kohathites must not enter the sacred tent while Aaron and his sons are covering the holy items. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [But they shall not enter the sacred tent]

The expression **when swallowing** is a common expression of this culture that means “even for a moment.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [even for a moment]

Here, **holy place** represents the things that belong in the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:15. Alternate translation: [the things that belong in the holy place]

The words **and die** express the result of touching the holy place. If it would be more natural in your language, you could make this connection more explicit. See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:15. Alternate translation: [which would cause them to die]

22.note: See how you translated this phrase in 4:2.

By **also them**, Moses means that he should count the descendants of Gershon in addition to having counted the descendants of Kohath. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in addition to the sons of Kohath]
See how you translated these phrases in 4:2.

23.q: מִ⁠בֶּן֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה וָ⁠מַ֗עְלָ⁠ה עַ֛ד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה
23.note: See how you translated this phrase in 4:3. Alternate translation: [From 30–50 years old]

The phrase **who comes to** is a common expression of this culture that means “who is able to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who can fight]

Here, Yahweh is speaking of serving in the tabernacle as if it were **fighting in the army**. This emphasizes that the work was strenuous and required careful coordination and attention to detail. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to be part of the group of workers]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to be in the army]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to serve what needs to be served]

Moses is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve carefully]

24.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [This is how the clans of the Gershonite serve]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **Gershonite**. He means all the descendants of Gershon in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Gershonites]

These phrases specify what exactly the service of the Gershonites was. It included both serving and carrying burdens. You could make this idea more explicit if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [both to serve and to carry their burdens]

25.note: Here, the word **Dwelling** refers specifically to the inner part of the sacred tent. The phrase **tent of meeting** refers specifically to the outer part of the sacred tent. See how you translated the similar phrases in 3:25. Alternate translation: [the curtains of the inner part of the Dwelling and the outer curtains of the Dwelling]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that the sacred tent had both an inner and an outer **covering**. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [its inner covering and the outer covering of porpoise which is on it]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 4:6.

The implication is that the covering being referred to was placed on top of the other coverings that were already on the tent. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on top of all these things]
See how you translated this phrase in 3:25.

26.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe an **opening** that is a **gate**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the opening that is the gate of]
See how you translated this clause in 3:26.

26.q: וְ⁠אֵת֙ מֵֽיתְרֵי⁠הֶ֔ם וְ⁠אֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבֹדָתָ֑⁠ם וְ⁠אֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵעָשֶׂ֛ה לָ⁠הֶ֖ם וְ⁠עָבָֽדוּ
26.note: Here, the pronouns **their** and **them** refer to the curtains for the sacred tent, and the pronoun **they** refers to the Gershonites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the ropes for the curtains and all the vessels of the curtain’s service and all that is done for the curtains; and the Gershonites shall serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vessels with which they are served]

The expression **is to be done** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is the Gershonites. Alternate translation: [all that the Gershonites do for them]

27.note: The phrase **upon the mouth of Aaron and his sons** is a common expression of his culture to mean “according to what Aaron and his sons command.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [According to what Aaron and his sons say]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how the sons of the Gershonite serve]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **Gershonite**. He means Gershonites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Gershonites]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and according to how they serve]
The word **you** is plural here because God is speaking to Moses and Aaron. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that Moses and Aaron are to assign specific tasks and equipment to specific people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated the similar phrase in 3:10. Alternate translation: [And you shall appoint]

By **all their burden in keeping**, Yahweh means everything that they must guard while they are carrying it. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [everything that they must guard as they carry it]

28.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [This is how the clans of the sons of the Gershonite serve]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **Gershonite**. He means the Gershonites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Gershonites]

Yahweh is using the common expression of his culture **in the hand of** to mean “under the authority of” or “under the supervision of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [under the control of]

29.q: בְּנֵ֖י מְרָרִ֑י לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֥⁠ם לְ⁠בֵית־אֲבֹתָ֖⁠ם תִּפְקֹ֥ד אֹתָֽ⁠ם
29.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about counting first, followed by the information about **their clans** and **the house of their fathers**. Alternate translation: [You shall count the sons of Merari, according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers]
See how you translated these phrases in 4:2.

The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. Alternate translation: [you, Moses, shall count]

30.note: See how you translated this phrase in 4:23.

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [to serve]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as the tent of meeting needs to be served]

31.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [according to how they serve]
See how you referred to these items in 3:36.

32.q: וְ⁠עַמּוּדֵי֩ הֶ⁠חָצֵ֨ר סָבִ֜יב וְ⁠אַדְנֵי⁠הֶ֗ם וִֽ⁠יתֵדֹתָ⁠ם֙ וּ⁠מֵ֣יתְרֵי⁠הֶ֔ם
32.note: See how you referred to these items in 3:37.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and for all the ways that they are served]

The phrase **by names** means that the priests were to assign specific items to specific people by recording each person’s name with the items he was to be responsible for. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and by each man’s name]
The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is speaking to Moses and Aaron. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
